account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. Its final beta test in late October 2024 ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded and Internet of Things devices. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target, generated and ran a fuzz test and exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer that a pointer still referenced. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in pull request 8139 on 1 November 2024. The fix shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024, and the release notes credit “Peter”. On 3 January 2025 the vendor's engineer Peter Samarin described the find on the company blog.

ai_role.statement: On the vendor's account, Spark selected the target, generated the fuzz test and ran it after a single “cifuzz spark” command. One manual step confirmed that the finding was real and exploitable under narrow conditions. wolfSSL's pull request and release notes confirm the bug, its location in pem_read_bio_key(), the timing and the reporter's first name. They mention neither AI nor Code Intelligence. The autonomous discovery therefore rests on the vendor's statements, repeated by QA Financial and SC Media, not on an independent test.

fields.account: Spark is the AI test agent in Code Intelligence GmbH's CI Fuzz product. Its final beta test in late October 2024 ran it on wolfSSL, an open-source cryptography library for embedded and Internet of Things devices. By the vendor's account, after one command the agent chose the target, generated and ran a fuzz test and exposed a heap use-after-free in pem_read_bio_key(). There a BIO write-back could reallocate a buffer that a pointer still referenced. The vendor reported it to wolfSSL, which merged a fix in pull request 8139 on 1 November 2024. The fix shipped in release 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024, and the release notes credit “Peter”. On 3 January 2025 the vendor's engineer Peter Samarin described the find on the company blog.

must_hold: A human must confirm the finding. The vendor says the one manual step was assessing that the bug exists and is exploitable under specific conditions
The beneficiary must be an identifiable project with a public fix record. Without wolfSSL's PR and release notes the event would rest on vendor claims alone

A sanitizer-detectable heap use-after-free in the BIO write-back path of pem_read_bio_key() that a generated input could trigger
A maintainer team that tracked the report as ZD#18875 and merged a fix within three days of the discovery

purpose: Spark was built to find bugs and vulnerabilities autonomously by selecting functions to fuzz and generating and running fuzz tests. Finding this flaw was exactly that function, exercised in the vendor's own beta test.

ratings.reason: wolfSSL received a reproducible report of a heap use-after-free in a path that parses private keys. It merged the fix within days, in pull request 8139 on 1 November 2024, and shipped it in 5.7.6 on 31 December 2024. The maintainers listed it among bug fixes, and the release's Vulnerabilities section does not include it. wolfSSL's vulnerabilities page lists no Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifier for it. The vendor itself says that the exploit conditions “don't seem easy to meet”, so the benefit is material and bounded.
